fit: verified original caffeine or outcome scope
assessment: The randomized waitlist trial allocated 67 participants with problematic use to immediate or delayed behavioral caffeine reduction. The manual addressed multiple source products. Primary results concerned caffeine intake rather than symptom efficacy. The discussion explicitly places prospective withdrawal-symptom trajectories outside the study. There is no separate fatigue result, fixed brewed-coffee arm or Parkinson fatigue comparison. The intake cohort is characterized in a related 2012 publication.

fit: verified original caffeine or outcome scope
assessment: The review discusses caffeine in coffee and tea, receptor effects, dependence and symptoms of withdrawal. It contrasts interpretations of acute arousal that may or may not depend on withdrawal. No new brewed-coffee Parkinson fatigue measurement is reported. Its Addicott reference, subjective tiredness items and other primary comparisons require separate family review.

fit: low-dose maintenance and blinded substitution
assessment: Reported fatigue is part of variable withdrawal after capsule cessation. Exact single-item estimate is unavailable.

fit: 24-hour and seven-day abstention
assessment: The abstract identifies tiredness as a sensitive measurement, with an alertness response only after shorter abstinence. Exact tiredness contrast is unavailable.

fit: blinded capsule replacement and fatigue threshold
assessment: The author abstract reports abnormally high POMS fatigue in 8% with placebo and 0% with usual intake or caffeine substitution under its threshold.

fit: blinded caffeine in habitual coffee drinkers
assessment: The abstract reports increased fatigue during deprivation. It does not establish overlap with an earlier related beverage cohort or isolate a brewed preparation.

fit: dependence reinforcement and acute substitution
assessment: More withdrawal symptoms, including fatigue, were reported after placebo following caffeine maintenance. Separate fatigue table remains open.

fit: controlled maintenance and acute fatigue item
assessment: The POMS fatigue item was highest after placebo challenged caffeine maintenance. The individual fatigue subscale contrast was narrower.

fit: usual-intake versus abstinent tiredness contrast
assessment: Subjective tiredness favored isolated caffeine under abstention. A comparable improvement was not established in usual-use state.

fit: intake interviews in the subsequent treatment cohort
assessment: The 94 treatment seekers reported prior withdrawal symptoms. The subsequent 67-person intervention drew from the same cohort and did not prospectively measure fatigue.

fit: manual-only taper and composite withdrawal syndrome
assessment: The pooled symptom score uses each person's maximum of five ratings, with one combining fatigue and drowsiness. No stand-alone randomized fatigue estimate appears.

fit: remote caffeine reduction registry and outcomes
assessment: The registered waitlist arms report named anxiety, sleep and GI outcomes plus a 19-item problem score. Fatigue has no separate posted endpoint.

fit: remote caffeine reduction article and aggregate symptoms
assessment: The author abstract lists named outcomes without a fatigue estimate. Enrollment and design align with the separate registry record.
